Sahara occidental : la Russie dévoile sa position avant le vote au Conseil de sécurité
items.description: Les déconvenues se multiplient pour le Maroc dans le dossier du Sahara occidental . Après le secrétaire général des Nations-Unies et son envoyé personnel, la Russie s'exprime en faveur de la reconduction du mandat de la mission des Nations-Unies pour l’organisation du référendum au Sahara occidental (Minurso), à quelques semaines de l'examen de la question par le Conseil de sécurité. Sahara occidental : l’ambassadeur d’Algérie à Moscou reçu par le vice-ministre russe des AE La position russe a été réitérée lors d'une rencontre vendredi 9 octobre à Moscou entre le vice-ministre russe des Affaires étrangères, Alexander Alimov, et l'ambassadeur d’Algérie en Russie, Toufik Djouama, à la demande de ce dernier. Au cours de l'entretien, les deux hommes ont abordé les principales questions relatives au Proche-Orient et à l'Afrique, “ sous l'angle de la coopération entre les deux pays au sein des Nations-unies ”, a indiqué le ministère russe des Affaires étrangères dans un communiqué. Une “ attention particulière ” a été accordée à la question du règlement du conflit du Sahara occidental, dans la perspective de l’examen, prévu ce mois d’octobre au Conseil de sécurité de l’ONU, des perspectives de prolongation du mandat de la Minurso, précise la même source. Sahara occidental : la Russie pour le maintien de la présence de l’ONU au Sahara occidental “ sous sa forme actuelle ” M. Alimov a souligné à l’ambassadeur d’Algérie à Moscou “ la constance de la position russe en faveur d’une solution juste, durable et mutuellement acceptable à la question du Sahara occidental, sur la base des résolutions pertinentes du Conseil de sécurité de l’ONU et dans le cadre des procédures conformes aux objectifs et principes de la Charte des Nations unies ”, lit-on dans le communiqué. “ L’importance du maintien de la présence de l’ONU sur le territoire non autonome sous sa forme actuelle a été soulignée, notamment pour préserver la stabilité ‘sur le terrain’ jusqu’à ce que le processus de règlement soit achevé ”, a ajouté la diplomatie russe, ce qui constitue un soutien franc de Moscou au renouvellement du mandat de la Minurso. Le Maroc a toujours œuvré pour le non-renouvellement du mandat de la Minurso étant donné que sa reconduction signifie que l’ONU demeure attachée au principe de l’autodétermination du peuple sahraoui via un référendum. Un vote sur cette question est prévu à la fin du mois d’octobre en cours au Conseil de sécurité. L’article Sahara occidental : la Russie dévoile sa position avant le vote au Conseil de sécurité est apparu en premier sur TSA .

items.title: Télétravail et santé mentale: les risques de l’hyperconnectivité
items.description: Derrière la souplesse du télétravail se cache un autre risque : celui de ne jamais vraiment décrocher. Isolement, sur-engagement et fatigue peuvent progressivement fragiliser les travailleurs. Le télétravail peut libérer du temps et réduire le stress lié aux déplacements, mais il peut aussi enfermer le travailleur dans une connexion permanente. Pour Ahmed Sakhir Ndiaye, psychologue du travail et enseignant à l’École normale supérieure d’enseignement technique et professionnel (Ensetp/Ucad), un télétravail mal encadré peut ainsi favoriser des risques psychosociaux (Rps) en situation de travail. « Si le télétravail offre une plus grande autonomie et réduit le stress lié aux transports à Dakar », il peut aussi créer, selon lui, « l’isolement social et organisationnel avec la perte des interactions formelles », ainsi qu’un problème d’équilibre entre vie professionnelle et vie personnelle. « Si le télétravail offre une plus grande autonomie et réduit le stress lié aux transports à Dakar, il peut aussi créer l’isolement social et organisationnel avec la perte des interactions formelles », Ahmed Sakhir Ndiaye Cette dégradation peut se traduire par plusieurs signaux d’alerte. Chez les managers, le psychologue, spécialiste en thérapie cognitive et comportementale, observe un « retrait progressif lors des réunions en ligne », des signes de « sur-engagement », avec des messages envoyés en dehors des heures de travail, ainsi que des « difficultés à prioriser ou à prendre des décisions simples ». Du côté des collaborateurs, la souffrance s’exprime par des « symptômes physiques et cognitifs comme des troubles du sommeil, des maux de tête récurrents ou de la fatigue persistante dès le réveil », accompagnés d’une nette « difficulté à fermer le bureau » et à se déconnecter de l’ordinateur. Pour prémunir les salariés contre le surmenage, Ahmed Sakhir Ndiaye préconise d’agir sur deux leviers. Sur le plan organisationnel, il invite les entreprises à « promouvoir un modèle de travail hybride et équilibré », en alternant travail à distance et présentiel. Il préconise également l’élaboration d’une « charte de déconnexion claire ». À l’échelle individuelle, le psychologue du travail conseille notamment d’aménager un espace dédié au travail, de planifier des pauses sans écran et d’instaurer une « routine de transition » en fin de journée pour marquer la rupture avec le monde professionnel. Fatou SY Le thème de la Journée mondiale de la santé mentale 2026, célébrée le 10 octobre, est : « À l’écoute de l’expérience vécue : des voix authentiques pour un réel changement »

items.title: 10 terrorists killed during CTD operation in Barkhan, says Balochistan govt
items.description: QUETTA: Ten terrorists were killed in a targeted intelligence-based operation conducted by the Counter-Terrorism Department (CTD) in Balochistan’s Barkhan district, the Home Department said on Saturday. An aide in the Home Department, Babar Yousafzai, said: “During an intense gun battle, 10 armed terrorists were killed and two CTD officials were injured.” The CTD had conducted a targeted operation after receiving credible information about the presence of terrorists belonging to the Indian proxy, Fitna al Hindustan , in the area, according to Yousafzai. The state has designated Balochistan-based terrorist groups as Fitna-al-Hindustan to highlight India’s alleged role in terrorism and destabilisation across Pakistan. Yousafzai added that the CTD had also seized a large quantity of arms, ammunition and explosives from the terrorists. According to other officials in the department, two CTD personnel were taken to a hospital, while the bodies of the terrorists were taken to the Rara Sham district hospital. Chief Minister Sarfraz Bugti paid rich tributes to the personnel of CTD for conducting the successful operation. He said that our brave security forces were playing an important role in the elimination of terrorism from Balochistan and rendering sacrifices to protect the lives and property of the people. On Oct 7, security forces killed five terrorists belonging to Fitna al-Hindustan i n Balochistan’s Mastung district, according to state media. Late last month, the military’s media affairs wing said that more than 71 terrorists had been killed in Shaban and other areas of Balochistan during 96 hours. On Sept 17, three terrorists were eliminated in an IBO in Balochistan’s Awaran district’s Badrang area. Another three were killed in Mastung on Sept 14. Earlier that month, 21 terrorists were killed in separate engagements in Nokcha, Chagai, Ziarat Cross, and Pishin. The number of terrorist attacks in the province increased by seven per cent from 83 in July to 89 in August, according to PICSS’ monthly assessment . As per the report, Balochistan was declared the province “most affected” by terrorism.

items.title: PM Shehbaz, Fazl speak on reducing tensions between Centre, KP govt
items.description: Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif on Saturday had a telephone call with Jamiat Ulema-i-Islam—Fazl (JUI-F) chief Maulana Fazlur Rehman, with reducing tensions between the Centre and the Khyber Pakhtunkhwa government among the topics discussed. According to a statement from the Prime Minister’s Office (PMO), PM Shehbaz congratulated the JUI-F leader on performing Umrah and extended an invitation for talks at the Prime Minister’s House. “Maulana Fazlur Rehman accepted the prime minister’s invitation [and] the meeting is expected to take place soon,” the statement read. The phone call follows recent contacts between Fazl, known for his engagement with politicians from across the board, and the opposition. The Oct 3 talks held to bridge differences between the Centre and the opposition alliance Tehreek-i-Tahafuz-i-Ayin-i-Pakistan (TTAP) failed due to multiple reasons , particularly the counterterrorism policy. On Tuesday, TTAP leaders called on Fazl at his residence, following which the veteran politician advised the federal government not to obstruct the PTI long march heading towards Islamabad, as protests were a democratic right enjoyed by all political parties. The next day, PM’s Adviser on Political Affairs Rana Sanaullah, Parliamentary Affairs Minister Tariq Fazal Chaudhry and National Assembly Speaker Ayaz Sadiq met the JUI-F chief. On Thursday, PTI MNA Junaid Akbar confirmed that Fazl had offered to play a role in ending the deadlock between the government and opposition, adding that the PTI’s “doors are open” to it. Speaking on Geo News , Akbar had said no framework had been put forward by Fazl regarding his role in the negotiations, although he noted that the JUI-F chief had been in touch with PTI leadership while he was away for Umrah. The same day, Defence Minister Khawaja Asif also hinted at efforts to restart negotiations between the Centre and the opposition, saying, “I wish a positive result comes out of the efforts of those involved in the talks. But, I have little hope.” Speaking to Dawn , JUI-F spokesman Aslam Ghauri said his party chief was playing the role of a “facilitator, not a mediator”. He distinguished the two roles by saying that a mediator would have the authority from opposition parties to make his own decision in light of their demands. “It is our (JUI-F’s) priority to bring both sides on table for resumption of talks,” he added, pointing out that they had urged the government to call a multi-party conference in Parliament House, where political and security issues should be discussed. The JUI-F leader said sitting at the table would benefit both sides, though the resumption of dialogue would mostly benefit the PTI because the KP government is “virtually being run by someone else and not by Chief Minister Sohail Afridi”. PM meets president Separately, PM Shehbaz also met with President Asif Ali Zardari, with the country’s overall security and political situation coming under discussion, according to an official handout. The premier was accompanied by Deputy Prime Minister and Foreign Minister Ishaq Dar, Adviser to the Prime Minister on Political Affairs Rana Sanaullah, Interior Minister Mohsin Naqvi, Attorney General Mansoor Usman Awan and Law Minister Azam Nazeer Tarar. “It was agreed during the meeting to convene separate sessions of the National Assembly and the Senate on Tuesday (Oct 13),” the statement said. Heightened tensions between Centre, PTI The PML-N-led federal government and the KP government led by PTI — which is in opposition in the Centre — have been at odds over various issues, particularly on the counterterrorism policy. The PTI has said it was being left out of security decisions concerning KP, which the Centre has denied . It also calls for reviewing the counterterrorism policy, while the latter criticises the KP government’s efforts to combat terrorism in the province and objects to its stance on dialogue with the Afghan Taliban. In recent days, federal ministers have assailed the PTI for staging a protest long march , which it has been warned against, at a time when KP faces security challenges. They have also linked differences over the counterterrorism policy with the possibility of an emergency or governor’s rule in KP. Earlier on Saturday, Information Minister Attaullah Tarar assailed the KP government over a “lack of governance” in the province, alleging that the provincial administration was given Rs700 billion under the National Finance Commission for development projects. “You did not upgrade the Counter Terrorism Department, did not establish forensic labs, did not install safe city cameras, which should be installed in the merged districts and all the entry-exit points of KP’s districts,” he alleged. On the other hand, the information minister claimed that the PTI was spending this money on organising protests.

items.title: GNAT pushes for clear implementation procedures of teachers’ conditions of service
items.description: The Ghana National Association of Teachers (GNAT) is pushing for clear procedures to guide the implementation of teachers’ conditions of service, warning that agreements risk remaining unfulfilled for years without a defined process for accessing the benefits. GNAT President Prosper Tachie said the union wants the Ministry of Education and the Ghana Education Service (GES) to finalise the procedures for implementing the provisions of the collective agreement before concluding outstanding negotiations. Speaking on JoyNews ‘ Newsfile, he said implementation had been a major challenge in previous agreements, with benefits often left hanging despite agreements being reached. “One of the major challenges confronting us so far as our collective agreement is concerned is about implementation. We will agree to the substantive document, but when it comes to procedural matters, as to how to assess the benefits within the document, we leave it hanging over the years, and this time round we are not ready for such a commitment,” he said. Mr Tachie said GNAT wanted the relevant authorities to specify how teachers would access the benefits provided under the agreement. “We want the Ministry of Education, Ghana Education Service, to finalise the document specifying processes of assessing certain benefits within the document,” he added. His comments follow the pre-tertiary teachers’ decision to suspend its nationwide strike after engagements involving the Labour Minister and the Council of State, alongside assurances from the government on outstanding demands. The government has committed to paying promotion-related arrears to more than 51,000 teachers by October 16. Payments relating to the professional development allowance and digital support allowance are expected in November and December, respectively. Mr Tachie said the union had also secured revised positions on some allowances following negotiations with the Fair Wages and Salaries Commission and the Ministry of Finance. He stressed that the suspension of the strike was interim, with discussions on outstanding provisions of the collective agreement expected to continue. Teachers are expected to return to the classrooms on Monday, October 12.

items.title: C’River govt shuts 58 unapproved schools in ongoing crackdown
items.description: The Cross River government says it has shut down no fewer than 58 unapproved schools in Calabar South, Calabar Municipality, Odukpani and Yakurr Local Government Areas (LGAs) of the state. The Commissioner for Education, Prof. Stephen Odey, disclosed on Saturday in Calabar. According to him, the ministry’s Department of Quality Assurance has intensified crackdown on schools operating without Approval to Operate (ATO) across the state. He noted that the exercise was part of the state’s ongoing efforts to sanitise the education sector, enforce compliance with established regulations, and ensure acceptable standards for teaching and learning. The commissioner further explained that the exercise was aimed at protecting learners and ensuring that schools operated in safe, conducive and properly regulated environments. Odey stressed that the government would not compromise the standards required for operating educational institutions in the state. The commissioner explained that the exercise was not intended to witch-hunt school proprietors, but rather, ensure that all schools met the prescribed minimal requirements for establishing and managing educational institutions. He urged proprietors of unapproved schools to regularise their operations by obtaining the necessary approval, warning that any school sealed by the government and reopened without authorisation would face appropriate sanctions. According to him, the enforcement exercise will continue across the state’s 18 LGAs until the objectives of the sector’s ongoing cleanup are achieved. Odey added that the exercise would be sustained across the state, in order to strengthen quality assurance, protect learners, as well as uphold the integrity of the education sector. items.title: Recurrent strikes threaten quality of education and academic calendars – Prof Bokpin
items.description: Economist and University of Ghana Business School Professor Gofred Bokpin has warned that recurrent labour strikes in Ghana’s education sector are undermining teaching time, academic calendars and the quality of graduates. Speaking on JoyNews’ Newsfile on Saturday, he said Ghana had experienced significant disruptions in the health and education sectors every two to three years over the past 15 to 20 years, describing the trend as a major concern for a country seeking sustained socio-economic development. Prof. Bokpin said lost instructional time could not be recovered, even when negotiations eventually led to the resolution of disputes. He argued that industrial harmony in education was essential to developing human capital, improving labour quality and supporting national development. Prof. Bokpin said the situation was particularly worrying for senior high schools operating under the Free Senior High School policy, where the double-track system and infrastructure constraints had already affected the time students spent in school. He warned that further disruptions could compromise the quality of education, adding that students were not receiving the level of tuition they needed while the state continued to provide for their upkeep. He also questioned the effectiveness of online learning as a substitute for classroom teaching when students on double-track arrangements returned home. The economist said universities were facing uncertainty over their academic calendars, noting that the Kwame Nkrumah University of Science and Technology (KNUST) had announced a postponement of its next academic year’s reopening. He said universities had worked to restore their academic calendars following the COVID-19 pandemic, but disruptions caused by industrial action were now creating further difficulties. While acknowledging that teachers, lecturers and administrators had demands that needed to be addressed, Prof. Bokpin said the government must prioritise industrial stability in the education sector. He argued that strikes often ended with negotiations and some concessions to workers, but the resulting loss of teaching time and productivity could not be reversed. Prof. Bokpin also cautioned against pursuing fiscal discipline at the expense of social priorities, saying government spending decisions should reflect the country’s development aspirations and the needs of its people. He urged the government to manage labour relations more effectively to protect the academic calendar and ensure that students receive quality education.

items.title: SEC ​‌‍‍‍‍⁠⁠‍​‌‍‍‍‍⁠⁠‌​DG urges universities to explore capital market funding
items.description: Nigerian universities have been urged to move away from dependence on government allocations and embrace capital formation, investment and ownership through the capital market. The call was made at the University of Ibadan Alumni Association Annual Public Service Lecture held on Friday in Ibadan. The lecture was themed: “First and Best But Whose Capital Built It? Rethinking How Nigeria Funds Its Own Future”. Delivering the lecture, the Director-General of the Securities and Exchange Commission (SEC), Dr Emomotimi Agama, traced the University of Ibadan foundation to an audacious capital decision. Agama recalled that in 1948, the chiefs and people of Ibadan donated 2,500 acres of land to the institution on a 999-year lease. He noted that despite producing a Nobel laureate, heads of state, central bank governors and builders of the capital market, the university had never approached the market to raise long-term funds. “Not once. Not a bond. Not a fund. Not a listed vehicle. “The premier university of Africa’s largest economy has been, financially speaking, a spectator at a market its own graduates built,” he said. Agama argued that continued dependence on government appropriations was unsustainable given the country’s current fiscal realities. He added that the university had about 41,700 students, while its halls of residence were built to accommodate fewer than 10,000, forcing thousands to live off-campus. The SEC director-general stressed that the problem was not a scarcity of capital in Nigeria but a failure to translate available capital into productive investments. He noted that pension assets stood at N31.48 trillion as of July 2026, while total market capitalisation on the Nigerian Exchange (NGX) stood at N215.09 trillion. Agama also contrasted the N4.65 trillion raised by banks over 24 months through recapitalisation with the N2.53 billion allocated to a university by the Tertiary Education Trust Fund (TETFund), representing a ratio of about 1,000 to one. According to him, the figures demonstrated that long-term capital was available and seeking bankable, long-term investment opportunities. Agama proposed five financing instruments that the university could explore under the Investments and Securities Act 2025. He said the first was a properly constituted endowment fund registered with the SEC as a collective investment scheme, with an independent trustee, a licensed fund manager and a spending rule of four to five per cent. The second, he said, was the issuance of bonds and sukuk through a ring-fenced vehicle backed by a defined, revenue-generating university asset. Agama described student housing as the most urgent opportunity for the university, proposing a Real Estate Investment Trust (REIT) or concession arrangement to convert rent currently paid by students to private landlords into a revenue stream for the institution. He also proposed a university innovation fund that would take equity stakes in spin-off companies emerging from its laboratories while enabling the institution to retain ownership of its research output. The SEC director-general added that the university could explore a diaspora-targeted investment instrument using the non-resident Bank Verification Number (BVN) framework to channel part of the $21.8 billion in annual remittances from consumption into investment. He, however, cautioned that accessing the capital market required financial discipline. He listed the requirements to include the annual publication of audited accounts, credit ratings by registered agencies, ring-fenced revenue streams that could withstand changes in leadership, and professional intermediation. Agama urged alumni to move from giving donations that were consumed to providing capital that could grow over time. He proposed an Alumni Capital Fund with a low minimum investment threshold to enable young graduates and Nigerians in the diaspora to participate, supported by transparent governance and annual audited accounts. In his remarks, the Acting President of the association, Prof. Terrumun Gajir, said the theme was timely as the country grappled with how to mobilise capital for sustainable prosperity. Gajir said Nigeria needed to deepen domestic investment and reduce excessive dependence on external capital. According to him, this requires mobilising pension funds, household savings and private capital for productive national development. He noted that a functional capital market would not only provide returns for investors but also support industries, infrastructure development and job creation. Gajir said the task before universities was to move from a culture of dependence to one of capital formation, investment, ownership and shared prosperity. Earlier, the Chairman of the occasion, Bayo Oyero, said the University of Ibadan should begin investing directly in financial markets beyond the activities of its alumni association. Oyero, an alumnus of the university, said the institution needed an independent endowment fund, separate from the existing Alumni Endowment Fund, which could be invested in properties and other assets to generate reasonable returns. He also called for the discussion to be extended to young Nigerians to encourage them to begin planning for their financial future early through investments in shares and stocks. (NAN) The post SEC ​‌‍‍‍‍⁠⁠‍​‌‍‍‍‍⁠⁠‌​DG urges universities to explore capital market funding appeared first on Vanguard News .

items.title: Sunday Igboho seeks stronger national alliance against kidnapping
items.description: By Adeola Badru Yoruba nation agitator and founder of Iru Ekun Security Network, Sunday Adeyemo, popularly known as Sunday Igboho, has called for a stronger national alliance between community-based security outfits and conventional security agencies to combat kidnapping, banditry and other violent crimes threatening communities across Nigeria. Igboho said closer cooperation among security stakeholders was essential to protecting lives and property, sharing intelligence and strengthening efforts to tackle criminal activities, particularly in the South-West. He made the call while commending the Inspector-General of Police, Tunji Disu, and other heads of security agencies for their support for Iru Ekun, which he said had contributed to the network’s reported efforts to address abduction, banditry and farmer-herder clashes. The call was contained in a statement issued by his media office on Saturday following a strategic meeting between the Commissioner of Police in the Federal Capital Territory (FCT), Ahmed Muhammed Sanusi, and the FCT coordinator of Iru Ekun, Segun Olufadeju, popularly known as Aluwaye, and members of his team in Abuja. According to the statement, the engagement was aimed at strengthening cooperation between the police and the security network in tackling criminality and promoting public safety. “The meeting with FCT CP, Ahmed Muhammed Sanusi, is part of our commitment to work with the Police and also show gratitude for their major support, which had been responsible for the success we have recorded in reducing rampant cases of abduction, banditry and farmers-herders clashes,” Igboho was quoted as saying. He added: “We are always ready to partner relevant stakeholders in the security sector in further driving peace, protecting communities against hoodlums and other criminals posing threat to our people, most especially law-abiding Nigerians in the South-West.” Igboho also acknowledged the support of the Minister of Defence, General Christopher Musa (rtd); the National Security Adviser, Nuhu Ribadu; the Inspector-General of Police, Tunji Disu; the Director-General of the Department of State Services (DSS), Adeola Oluwatosin Ajayi; and other heads of security agencies. “The Minister of Defence, General Christopher Musa (rtd), National Security Adviser, Nuhu Ribadu, IGP Tunji Disu, the Director-General of the DSS, Adeola Oluwatosin Ajayi, and other heads of security agencies have all been supportive and instrumental to our operational achievements.” “We will continue to leverage on this healthy collaboration for the overall interest of Nigeria,” he said. At the meeting, Sanusi urged Iru Ekun to sustain effective working relationships with the police, the Nigerian Armed Forces, the DSS and other paramilitary agencies, describing inter-agency cooperation as critical to community policing and the effectiveness of local security initiatives. The FCT police commissioner also stressed that the network should notify relevant security agencies, particularly divisional police authorities within its areas of operation, before undertaking security activities requiring operational action. He said such coordination was necessary to improve crime prevention and detection and ensure that community-based security initiatives worked in collaboration with established security institutions. Responding, Olufadeju pledged that the network would consistently inform and engage the police in the FCT about its activities. The post Sunday Igboho seeks stronger national alliance against kidnapping appeared first on Vanguard News .

items.title: ‘Cockroach’ group leaders among hundreds detained in Delhi protest
items.description: Hundreds of protesters have reportedly been detained in Delhi during the latest demonstration by the Gen-Z led Cockroach Janta Party (CJP) over electoral reforms. The group said its founder Abhijeet Dipke, who began the movement in May after India’s Chief Justice likened some jobless young people to “cockroaches”, was detained with other leaders shortly after landing in Delhi. Tens of thousands of security personnel were deployed and roads barricaded ahead of the demonstration, though the CJP insisted it would go ahead. Delhi Police has not commented on the detentions, but had refused permission for the protest to take place at Jantar Mantar, a landmark in the Indian capital. The group – who are not registered as a political party in India – are seeking electoral reforms just months before crucial state elections. It has also demanded the resignation of Chief Election Commissioner (CEC) Gyanesh Kumar over allegations of manipulating voters’ lists – which the Election Commission has denied. Under Kumar’s leadership, India’s election commission has undertaken a mammoth exercise to update electoral rolls nationwide – it said this was a routine exercise to weed out dead, duplicate or ineligible voters. But in many states, the exercise has been shrouded in controversy, with tens of thousands of people alleging they have been wrongly removed. The CJP – and opposition parties – accuse Kumar of favouring Prime Minister Narendra Modi’s Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP) in the way the electoral rolls are being updated. The Election Commission and the BJP have denied this. Before arriving in Delhi, the CJP’s founder Dipke said: “If you think you can stop us by threatening us with jail or trying to intimidate us with the fear of imprisonment, you are mistaken.” He and and two other leaders, Saurav Das and Ashutosh Ranka, were detained on their flight from Mumbai on Saturday. The group claimed the three men have been taken to an undisclosed location. Delhi Police have not commented. Ajinkya Shinde, the CJP’s new designated leader while the others are in detention, released a video telling protesters that “if Delhi Police tries to stop you, wherever they stop you will become your Jantar Mantar”. Student activist Neha Bora, who had also been detained by Delhi Police, urged demonstrators to “hold the line”. The large number of protesters expected to descend on Delhi were unable to get anywhere close to Jantar Mantar due to the heavy security presence and road blocks. Announcements could be heard across the city, asking people to co-operate with the police. One protester, Sabika Muzaffar, told the BBC she and her mother expected to be detained. “On the way to the protest site, instead of reciting hymns and verses as we usually do, my mother and I were rote learning our lawyer’s number,” she said. She said that showing up to protest was “her way of defending the country and its democracy”. A few minutes after Muzaffar spoke to the BBC she was taken away by police. Several trains to and from major Delhi stations had been cancelled and dozens of metro stations were closed from Friday night. Buses packed with detained protesters were seen being driven away from the protest site. The CJP first emerged as a major protest movement during weeks of demonstrations over the summer demanding education reforms and the resignation of Education Minister Dharmendra Pradhan. The group stemmed from a joke made by Dipke in response to a remark by India’s Chief Justice Surya Kant, who had likened jobless youngsters to “cockroaches”. He later said the comments were misinterpreted. Dipke, who previously worked with the opposition Aam Aadmi Party (AAP), had just completed a master’s degree at Boston University when he posted a question on X in May: “What if all cockroaches come together?” The post went viral, and the CJP was born. Momentum built around the movement which tapped into anger over over unemployment, exam paper leaks and government accountability. In July, Dipke watched from the stage as the five-week-long protest ended in celebration after the resignation of India’s education minister.

items.title: Denmark allows citizens of 9 countries visa-free entry under biometric passport rule
items.description: Denmark allows citizens of nine countries to enter the country without a visa if they hold qualifying biometric passports, although the exemption is part of the country’s existing immigration rules rather than a newly announced policy. The countries are Albania, Bosnia and Herzegovina, Georgia, Kosovo, Moldova, Montenegro, North Macedonia, Serbia and Ukraine, according to the Danish Immigration Service’s official visa guidance. Full list of the 9 countries According to the Danish Immigration Service, citizens of the following countries qualify for visa-free entry when they meet the applicable biometric passport requirements. Albania: Citizens holding qualifying biometric passports are exempt from the visa requirement. Bosnia and Herzegovina: Holders of biometric passports can enter Denmark without a visa. Georgia: Biometric passport holders qualify, although the exemption does not cover diplomatic, service, official or special passports under the stated rules. Kosovo: Citizens with biometric passports qualify for the exemption. Moldova: Holders of biometric passports are exempt from the visa requirement. Montenegro: Citizens holding qualifying biometric passports can travel without a visa. North Macedonia: Biometric passport holders qualify for visa-free entry. Serbia: Citizens with biometric passports are exempt, subject to the applicable exceptions. Ukraine: Citizens holding biometric passports qualify for the exemption. What is a biometric passport? A biometric passport, also known as an electronic passport or e-passport, contains an electronic chip holding information used to verify the travel document holder’s identity. Such passports are used in international travel to support identity verification and strengthen document security. For citizens of the nine countries, possessing the qualifying passport means they do not need to obtain a Danish short-stay visa before travelling, provided they meet the applicable entry requirements. items.title: Tuteur légal de l’élève : le ministère de l’Éducation dément l’exclusion des mères
items.description: Qui est le tuteur légal de l'élève habilité à ce titre à entrer en contact avec les établissements scolaires en Algérie ? La question a fait débat sur les réseaux sociaux ces derniers jours après le partage de notes de certains établissements scolaires déniant aux mères le statut de tuteur. Le ministère de l’Éducation nationale a tenu à clarifier les choses. « Aucune instruction » privant les mères du suivi de la scolarité de leurs enfants Dans un communiqué diffusé ce samedi 10 octobre, le ministère dément avoir publié des instructions privant les mères de la possibilité de suivre la scolarité de leurs enfants dans les établissements d'enseignement. « Ces obligations incombent aux parents dans le cadre de leur accord avec l'établissement d'enseignement concernant le parent en charge de cette responsabilité », précise le département de Mohamed Seghir Saadaoui. Les parents doivent s'informer, en ce qui concerne leur relation avec l’établissement scolaire, sur le site officiel du ministère ou sur les pages officielles des directions de l'éducation, rappelle le communiqué. « Une responsabilité institutionnelle partagée » « Le suivi des progrès scolaires des élèves et l'attention portée à leurs résultats scolaires, à leur discipline et à leur comportement en milieu scolaire constituent une responsabilité institutionnelle partagée », souligne le ministère, assurant que, dans ce contexte, il accueille les parents dans tous ses établissements d’enseignement « comme des partenaires qui l’accompagnent pour assurer la sérénité et la discipline nécessaires à nos enfants au sein des établissements scolaires ». La mise au point fait suite au partage de notes d’établissements indiquant que le tuteur légal de l'élève est le père. Dans un de ces documents, attribué à un lycée de la wilaya d’El Oued, il a été fait état de « problèmes causés au sein de l’établissement par des mères d'élèves », précisant que la mère ne peut être le tuteur légal que dans certains cas, comme le décès du père, son emprisonnement, le divorce ou l'accord écrit du père. Le document n’a pas fait l’objet d’un démenti de l’établissement concerné. L’article Tuteur légal de l’élève : le ministère de l’Éducation dément l’exclusion des mères est apparu en premier sur TSA .

items.title: UK universities withdraw admission offers to Nigerians over visa crackdown
items.description: Universities in the United Kingdom are withdrawing admission offers to international applicants, including Nigerians and Pakistanis, amid fears that rising student visa refusals could lead to a ban on recruiting overseas students. According to an analysis of Home Office data by the Financial Times, 22.7 per cent of study visa applications from Nigerians were withdrawn in the first half of 2026, up from 4.5 per cent in the same period of 2025. For Pakistani applicants, the proportion rose from three per cent to 40.9 per cent, while Bangladesh’s rate increased from 7.1 per cent to 23.5 per cent. Overall, withdrawn applications rose to 10.5 per cent in the first half of 2026, compared with 2.3 per cent a year earlier. Universities said the withdrawals were largely driven by a doubling of student visa refusals in the first six months of 2026, alongside stricter rules that put institutions at risk of losing their licences to recruit international students if more than five per cent of applicants with offers have their visa applications rejected. About 15 universities are believed to have suspended recruitment from Pakistan this year, while data from visa-processing company Enroly suggests that refusal rates at almost half of universities exceed the five per cent threshold. Sir David Bell, vice-chancellor of the University of Sunderland, said: “The recent and unexpected spike in visa refusals has prompted pre-emptive action in several universities. This has involved pulling back from international markets where a tougher approach is being taken to visa applications.” Jamie Arrowsmith, director of Universities UK International, said “visa processing has become markedly less predictable”. “Many refusals appear to rest on flawed, inconsistent and highly subjective reasoning, forcing universities to withdraw offers at scale to avoid breaching compliance thresholds,” he added. The crackdown has raised concerns about universities’ finances as institutions face declining international applications and growing competition for overseas students. Vanessa Wilson, chief executive of University Alliance, warned: “This is going to result in restructures, which inevitably results in job losses, course closures, campus closures.” Universities have also questioned the reasons given for some visa refusals, including cases involving applicants who had previously considered studying in other countries. Professor Steven McGuire, deputy vice-chancellor of the University of East Anglia, said his institution began withdrawing offers from certain countries late last year following a sharp rise in refusals. “We were getting some very arbitrary and ill-informed refusals,” he said. “We had one where the interviewer did not seem to understand that UEA was in Norwich [and so rejected the applicant for not knowing where they were going to study].” McGuire warned that the policy could push universities to “double down on China and India”, where refusal rates are lower, adding that institutions were “running out of options except a very significant resizing of the sector”. Professor James Miller, vice-chancellor of the University of the West of Scotland, said some refusals were “extremely spurious” and that the Home Office had offered “no real explanation [for the increase] other than concern about number of students claiming asylum”. He added that some universities had “stopped recruiting from certain geographical areas to keep refusal rates below 5 per cent”. Miller warned that many institutions could record a decline of more than 20 per cent in overseas student numbers this year, making job cuts “inevitable” without a policy change. “It’s harming the UK’s reputation, it’s contrary to other government policies and at an individual level it’s denying opportunity to people who want to advance their careers and their lives,” he said. The Home Office said international students “make a positive contribution” to Britain, but added that “this must not be at the expense of recruiting responsibly, in turn protecting the integrity of our immigration system”. It said it was offering universities “support where needed to improve recruitment practices”. items.title: Those Books of Smut and Wonder
items.description: Do your heroes weep? Do they swoon with lust? Are they really confused by their new magical powers? Then you’re already a fan of romantasy. For those still waiting to discover romantasy: It’s fantasy, with strong female protagonists and fewer boring bits—the long treks over major landforms in hard weather. Sex is plentiful, but sex is not the genre’s defining feature. You can go chapters before encountering a reference to someone’s toned body. Far more significant are feelings and friendships between the heroes: enchanted beings with relatable self-esteem issues who don’t just seek and fight but also yearn and banter as they face down enemies who aren’t only evil, but super bitchy too. Then the heroes cry and have orgasms (sometimes they orgasm first and cry after). In the kingdom of romantasy, one writer reigns supreme: Sarah J. Maas, the author of ACOTAR . It sounds like a missile-defense system or an autoimmune condition, but it’s the acronym for one of the most popular series of novels for adults written in the 21st century. A Court of Thorns and Roses is the first of many books about Feyre Archeron, a young huntress spirited into the faerie realm. Humans hate the leaders of the faerie world, called the High Fae, who once enslaved them. But as soon as one bursts through Feyre’s door, having shape-shifted into the body of a green-eyed, bearlike beast, the reader thinks, I bet some of these guys are going to be hot . Feyre falls in love and breaks a curse and brings down a depraved fae queen, and that’s just in the first book—eventually she’ll assemble a crew of beloved sidekicks and a heap of supernatural powers. On any given week, you can see every book in the series stacked in a column on the New York Times best-seller list. If you combine ACOTAR with Maas’s two other series, Throne of Glass and Crescent City , she has sold some 75 million copies. The Lord of the Rings has likely sold more than twice that, but J. R. R. Tolkien had a 60-year head start. After A Court of Thorns and Roses come courts of: Mist and Fury , Wings and Ruin , Frost and Starlight , and Silver Flames . Fans waited five long years for the sixth book. Would the next court have one syllable and two syllables? Would the decent faeries stop the awful ones from slaughtering and re-enslaving the humans? Then Maas announced, in a rare interview on the podcast Call Her Daddy , that she would actually be releasing three new books—one in October, one in January, and one more after that—and people lost their minds. Right away a question shot into the inboxes of America’s bookstores: Are you having a midnight release party? Tickets sold out. For one “fantasy ball” at a bookstore in El Paso, Texas, they sold out in 12 hours. A second party was announced; it sold out too. Book clubs began rereading all of the courts in preparation. [ Read: The publishing industry’s most swoon-worthy genre ] On social media, bets were made about which of Feyre’s sisters or friends the new books would focus on, and what color the covers would be (Maas hadn’t done purple yet). In August, images of the next two jackets—­for A Court of Splintered Harmony and A Court of Forgotten Melody — lit up Times Square . They were ombré! But search The New York Review of Books or the London Review of Books for Maas, and you’ll find references to a German foreign minister, a river, the Pynchon character Oedipa Maas —and no trace of Sarah J. The New Yorker ’s culture podcast summed up the low end of romantasy as “customer service wrapped in self-care wrapped in literature,” though one of the critics admitted that she’d loved A Court of Thorns and Roses . Hear enough writers lament that the only books that sell now are faerie or dragon or elfpunk porn, and you start to get the feeling that the literary establishment is committed to resenting this rare bright spot in the publishing industry. Maas, now 40, was a teenager when she wrote an epic fairy tale about a young assassin who can slit throats as well as waltz at balls for a fiction site. That story was published by Bloomsbury, in 2012, as Throne of Glass . The novels that followed took off on #BookTok and then in real life thanks to a generation of former Harry Potter fans who now had jobs, babies, and stymied sex drives. These people (women) started reading (or listening). They started going to bookstores. Fewer Americans are reading for pleasure every year, and yet people keep opening bookstores—romance bookstores in particular ( more than 100 in the past year and a half alone , according to the American Booksellers Association). Zella Funk­houser, a high-school science teacher, runs three book clubs at the newly opened Bonfire Bookstore & Yarnery, in Shenandoah County, Virginia. She told me that she picked up A Court of Thorns and Roses in 2023, after having gone “years without really reading a whole lot.” Then back-to-back snowstorms hit, and her husband, who does road work for the state, spent days out plowing. Alone at home behind a wall of snow, Funkhouser devoured all five books. “We didn’t have internet; we didn’t have power,” she told me. “I was obsessed.” On a Saturday night in June, her book club discussed Thorns and Roses . Erin was reading the series for the third time, Tiffani for the fourth, Abby for the fifth. “We’re not reading high literature, let’s be honest,” one of the women acknowledged. But they weren’t looking for formal innovation; they were looking to be inspired and turned on. It’s true that you’re rarely transported by ACOTAR ’s language. Characters say things like “I admire your balls, Feyre.” Sometimes they make me laugh. “Shall we assist you, or just flap here, talking?” a leader of winged reinforcements asks, when it seems the battle has been lost. Characteristic of the genre, the books remix familiar stories. The first meal in Beauty and the Beast , minus the dancing silverware. Pride and Prejudice , if the lovers started out on even worse terms. Hades and Persephone, if the king of the underworld just really got you. But even if you don’t read romantasy (I don’t read romantasy), the books are well crafted and very entertaining. And for its hard-core fans, ACOTAR has achieved something like a vertical integration of the imagination: the raw fiber of old myths woven into new stories, processed through the internet, refined into audiobooks for intimate delivery straight down the ear canal, which drive fans back to bookstores, where they can buy a keepsake hardcover and even, if they’re lucky, drink themed cocktails in ACOTAR -inspired ball gowns at midnight. With this kind of power, Maas doesn’t need the literary establishment. (Bloomsbury, her publisher, declined to share advance copies of the new novels with me.) At one point, Maas puts her toughest character alone in a library. She’s full of rage and a terrible power. And—take this, haters—she’s reading a smutty romance. In the Call Her Daddy interview, with her high cheekbones and golden hair and bare feet tucked beneath her, Maas looked a bit like one of her own characters as she talked about her “useless” creative-writing degree and recalled telling a professor, “I will never fucking write a poem.” She couldn’t understand “the meter and the rhythm” and had to ask her math-major boyfriend (now husband) for help. But when you read about a battle ending with enchanted water bubbling from “the lips of all the Hybern soldiers as Tarquin drowned them on dry land,” you suspect she knows what meter is, even if she doesn’t care what it’s called. She’s got a line of nearly perfect iambs there. Enough about language. We’ve gone too long without talking about sex, and Maas would not approve. Sometimes she makes you wait for it (faeries, who are basically immortal, can spend centuries edging) but then, before you know it, someone’s getting a blow job in the dining room. The books get dirtier as they go. Reading on the subway about Feyre coming so hard that she “couldn’t tell where one climax ended and the second began,” I might have been less embarrassed to be caught watching actual porn. I really wished that one crucial sex scene hadn’t involved so much wet paint. Maas’s characters are often splattered with something: mud, blood, stardust, semen (but only by Book 5). Still, there’s this one scene: Feyre—degraded, but into it—and a throne room, and a thumb moving in lazy circles … I’ll say it. I’m just going to say it. I liked it. Smut aside, what really matters is how the charac­ters grow together. You keep reading to see if they track down the enchanted artifacts but also to find out if true romantic partnerships are possible, the kind where care is taken and respect given. In the real world, many women are profoundly disappointed by and mistrustful of men. You might assume that this is why so many women are suddenly so eager to fantasize about another species entirely. But, fundamentally, these books are stories of friendship and love. Why should the novels’ popularity suggest that women are giving up on men? It could mean they’re holding out hope. Maybe, eventually, more than a handful of men will read these books. After all, I was raised on the paperback heroes of my father’s epics: The Lord of the Rings , The Wheel of Time . And Harry Potter , of course. Being a girl didn’t stop me from wanting the boy to save the world. I remember listening to The Sorcerer’s Stone in the car as a child, on road trips with my family, when things were not so good, when things were sometimes pretty bad, and seeing, not the tense edge of each parent’s opposing shoulder, but the night sky across the ensorcelled ceiling of the Hogwarts dining hall. Romantasy readers know they’re not actually going to “go out and find dragons and magic,” Funk­houser said, but if they’re snowed in—­or trapped by a pandemic, or up with a nursing newborn, or stuck in any of the ways humans tend to get stuck—­it can help to imagine they could. Some books make you want to be a better writer or thinker, some books make you want to be a better person, and some books make you glad to be reading them. There may be a ceiling on what this literature can do. But it’s an enchanted one. This article appears in the November 2026 print edition with the headline “Those Books of Smut and Wonder.”

Govt assails PTI over 'lack of governance' in Khyber Pakhtunkhwa
items.description: Information Minister Attaullah Tarar on Saturday assailed the PTI-led Khyber Pakhtunkhwa government over a “lack of governance” in the province. Addressing a press conference in Islamabad, he alleged that the provincial government was given Rs700 billion under the National Finance Commission for development projects. “You did not upgrade the Counter Terrorism Department (CTD), did not establish forensic labs, did not install safe city cameras, which should be installed in the merged districts and all the entry-exit points of KP’s districts,” he alleged. On the other hand, the information minister claimed that the PTI was spending this money on organising protests. “You don’t even give half an hour to discuss terrorism in the province, but you organise six-hour meetings to spread turmoil and vandalism,” he criticised. Tarar further said that the PTI had “trapped” millions of people in the province to get its leader, former prime minister Imran Khan, released from jail. “You trapped them in poverty, in disease by not providing the adequate health facilities, in ignorance by not providing educational opportunities, and in non-development by not improving infrastructure,” he said. Tarar also alleged that the KP government had held the people of the province “captive to terrorists”. “From the very first day, this is my opinion that they [PTI] are the B-team of the Tehreek-i-Taliban Pakistan,” Tarar said. The information minister said that the PTI facilitated terrorists in settling in the country. “For how long will it go on? That the security forces will clear the area of terrorists and establish peace, but you will bring the terrorists back?” he asked. During his address, Tarar said that the PTI government in KP had dragged the province into the “stone age” during the last 13 and a half years. Citing various federal government projects, Tarar maintained that there was no comparison of the hours spent working by Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif and KP Chief Minister Sohail Afridi to address governance issues and take relief and reform measures. He said that the chief ministers of all the provinces were working hard, questioning how many hours Afridi spent on governance. “Tell us if you have ever given a big hospital, a university, a highway to your people, an information technology project to the youth of KP or given them laptops or gadgets,” he said. “How long can such a system, where there is chaos and extremist politics, continue?” he asked. He claimed that the KP government wanted to hand over the province to terrorists as it prioritised “personal interests over the national interests”. “This province needs peace, not politics,” Tarar stated. Asked about imposing an emergency or governor’s rule in KP, Tarar said that responding to this question would be premature. “Everyone is asking how long KP and its people will remain at the mercy of its government,” he said. “In my opinion, the conditions in KP have never been worse. They could not be worse than this. What’s worse than terrorists roaming in the streets? You have designated no-go areas in most of your districts because you collect ransom in collusion with terrorists,” he claimed. He said that the people of KP go to Punjab or other provinces for medical treatment. “Will there ever come a time when people from across Pakistan go to KP for treatment?” he asked. The information minister asserted that the PTI would not be allowed to destroy the province. Addressing the same press conference, Coordinator to the Prime Minister on Information for KP Affairs Ikhtiar Wali Khan also questioned the lack of development in the province. “Universities are shutting down because there are no vice chancellors there. Eighteen out of 34 universities in KP are on the verge of bankruptcy,” he said. Wali said that people complained about the lack of good roads in Karachi. “But when people of KP go to Karachi, they say that Karachi’s roads are much better than KP.” Calling on the people and journalists in KP, Wali urged them to talk about the “ground realities”, claiming that the people were crying over the existing health facilities in the province. He referred to the KP police as the shuhada force, alleging that the provincial government had left them unarmed. He alleged that the PTI government had seized the money allocated to fund the CTD to combat terrorism. Wali also accused KP ministers of corruption and bad governance in the province. “The people of KP need peace, health facilities and a political culture based on tolerance, acceptance and respect,” he said. The PML-N-led federal government and the KP government led by PTI — which is in opposition in the Centre — have been at odds over various issues, particularly on the counterterrorism policy. This was also a key reason behind the breakdown of the Oct 3 talks between them. The PTI has said it was being left out of security decisions concerning KP, which the Centre has denied . It also calls for reviewing the counterterrorism policy, while the latter criticises the KP government’s efforts to combat terrorism in the province and objects to its stance on dialogue with the Afghan Taliban. Kundi, Muqam discuss KP’s security and political situation In Peshawar, Minister for Kashmir Affairs and Gilgit Baltistan Amir Muqam met KP Governor Faisal Karim Kundi at Governor House, where they discussed the overall law and order situation in the province. According to a joint statement issued after the meeting, the two leaders also discussed the PTI’s long march and exchanged views on issues of mutual interest, particularly the political environment in the province. Kundi and Muqam thanked the people of KP, saying they had rejected the politics of unrest and confrontation. They reiterated that the federal government would continue taking all possible measures to restore lasting peace, strengthen security and accelerate public welfare and development in the province. The two leaders also observed that the people of KP had grown frustrated with terrorism and what they described as political elements promoting instability, reaffirming the federal government’s commitment to ensuring peace and stability in the province. In a post on X, Kundi said, “Our people have paid an unbearable price in the war against terrorism. They cannot be held hostage to the politics of anarchy and agitation.” He affirmed that the federal government “will continue to take all possible measures to strengthen security, protect our people and support the province’s development”. “The future of KP cannot be sacrificed at the altar of political ambition,” the governor declared. “This province does not need any more political stunts that undermine security and endanger lives. I commend the people of KP for standing with peace,” he wrote. In recent days, federal ministers have assailed the PTI for staging a protest long march , which it has been warned against, at a time when KP faces security challenges. They have also linked differences over the counterterrorism policy with the possibility of an emergency or governor’s rule in KP. On Friday, Parliamentary Affairs Minister Dr Tariq Fazal Chaudhry said the government had finished deliberating on the imposition of an emergency and warned that it would avail the option if the KP government did not cooperate on counterterrorism. Gohar meets CM Afridi On the other hand, PTI Chairman Barrister Gohar Ali Khan said on X that he met CM Afridi in Peshawar to discuss the country’s political situation, the party’s long march and “other important matters”. PTI Secretary General Salman Akram Raja, MNA Junaid Akbar, Parliamentary Leader Shahid Kattak and KP Information Minister Shafi Jani were also present during the meeting. Speaking to reporters after the meeting, Gohar said the imposition of governor’s rule or an emergency was not the right solution to the province’s issues, considering the “circumstances”. The PTI chairman said there were no conflicting views on eradicating terrorism, but rather on the method of doing so, which could be resolved. “Those who have taken up swords against the state [and[ those who are enemies of the state are our enemies; if they can be eradicated by imposing governor’s rule or an emergency, we would welcome it, but this would further deteriorate the situation,” Gohar said. He called on the country’s political leadership to “demonstrate political wisdom” and said a meeting of either the federal or provincial apex committee should be called if any situation required the imposition of governor’s rule.

items.title: Top 8 most innovative countries in Africa in 2026
items.description: Africa’s most innovative countries are investing in technology, research, entrepreneurship and industrial development as they seek to strengthen their economies and compete in the global market. From mobile money and financial technology to automotive manufacturing and artificial intelligence, countries across the continent are adopting different approaches to innovation. While some are building on established research institutions and industrial capacity, others are using digital solutions to tackle challenges in finance, agriculture, healthcare and public services. However, the pace of innovation varies considerably across the continent. Access to investment, skilled workers, research facilities and reliable infrastructure continues to influence the ability of countries to develop new technologies and turn ideas into commercially successful products. The World Intellectual Property Organisation’s (WIPO) Global Innovation Index 2026 provides a framework for comparing innovation performance across economies. According to the rankings and scores provided, Mauritius leads the African countries featured, followed by Morocco and South Africa. Here are the 10 most innovative countries in Africa in 2026, based on their reported Global Innovation Index rankings and scores. 1. Mauritius — Score: 34.1 Global rank: 50th Mauritius ranks first among the African countries on the list, reflecting its efforts to develop an economy driven by financial services, technology and entrepreneurship. The island nation has cultivated a business environment that supports investment and private-sector development. Its financial services industry and growing digital economy provide opportunities for businesses to adopt new technologies and develop innovative products. Mauritius is also working to reduce its dependence on traditional economic activities by encouraging investment in emerging sectors. Its relatively developed business ecosystem and venture capital activity contribute to its position as a destination for entrepreneurs and investors seeking opportunities in Africa. 2. Morocco — Score: 32.8 Global rank: 54th Morocco’s innovation performance is closely linked to its expanding industrial base and efforts to attract international investment. The country has established itself as an important manufacturing destination, particularly in the automotive and aerospace industries. These sectors encourage the development of technical expertise, advanced production methods and closer collaboration between local businesses and international manufacturers. Its proximity to European markets also provides opportunities for industrial partnerships and technology transfers. By investing in manufacturing capabilities, education and industrial development, Morocco is seeking to move further up global value chains and expand its role in technology-driven production. 3. South Africa — Score: 30.9 Global rank: 63rd South Africa benefits from a comparatively mature research environment, developed financial markets and an established technology sector. Cities such as Johannesburg and Cape Town host companies operating in financial technology, software development, biotechnology and renewable energy. The country’s universities and research institutions also provide a foundation for scientific research and the development of new technologies. Its established corporate sector creates opportunities for businesses to commercialise research and expand innovative products into regional and international markets. Nevertheless, persistent infrastructure challenges, electricity supply constraints and difficulties in translating research into commercially successful products remain obstacles. Addressing these issues could help South Africa strengthen its innovation ecosystem and improve the competitiveness of local businesses. 4. Tunisia — Score: 29.3 Global rank: 71st Tunisia draws on its engineering expertise and technical education system to support innovation across information technology, electronics and manufacturing. The country’s skilled workforce offers opportunities for businesses seeking technical services and specialised talent. Its geographical proximity to Europe also creates opportunities for partnerships involving technology, manufacturing and business services. Entrepreneurs are increasingly exploring digital solutions for businesses and consumers, while the country’s technical skills provide a foundation for further development. Expanding access to investment and creating stronger links between research institutions and private businesses could help Tunisia translate more of its technical expertise into commercially viable innovations. 5. Botswana — Score: 27.1 Global rank: 82nd Botswana is working to broaden its economic base beyond diamond mining by encouraging entrepreneurship, technology adoption and private-sector growth. Digital financial services and technology-enabled business solutions offer opportunities to improve productivity in sectors beyond mining. The country’s relatively stable institutions also provide a foundation for businesses seeking to invest in new ventures. However, Botswana’s innovation ecosystem remains relatively small compared with those of Africa’s larger technology markets. Expanding access to funding, supporting technology startups and developing specialised skills will be important to its efforts to build a more diversified economy. 6. Egypt — Score: 26.1 Global rank: 83rd Egypt’s large domestic market, substantial pool of graduates and expanding digital economy provide opportunities for innovation across several industries. Its startup ecosystem includes businesses developing financial technology, e-commerce platforms and digital services. These companies are using technology to improve transactions, connect consumers with businesses and create new ways of delivering services. Technology parks and entrepreneurship programmes also seek to support emerging businesses, while the country’s universities provide a source of technical and professional talent. Egypt’s ability to turn these advantages into stronger innovation outcomes will depend partly on access to investment, support for research and the growth of businesses capable of competing beyond the domestic market. 7. Senegal — Score: 24.4 Global rank: 90th Senegal is building an innovation ecosystem around digital services, entrepreneurship and financial inclusion. Its capital, Dakar, has developed into an important centre for technology startups, including businesses creating payment platforms and digital solutions for communities with limited access to traditional financial services. Technology is also creating opportunities to improve business operations and expand access to services. Investment and international partnerships have further supported interest in the country’s emerging technology sector. For Senegal, strengthening links between startups, investors and established businesses could help promising ideas reach more customers and contribute more substantially to economic development. 8. Rwanda — Score: 23.3 Global rank: 96th Rwanda has pursued technology adoption and public-sector reforms as part of its broader economic development strategy. Kigali is the centre of much of the country’s entrepreneurship and technology activity, with initiatives aimed at encouraging investment, expanding digital services and improving access to financial products. Technology is also being applied to public services and business operations, demonstrating how digital tools can support development beyond the private sector. items.title: Palestinian president postpones legislative elections to September 2027
items.description: Palestinian President Mahmoud Abbas on Saturday postponed legislative elections to September next year, official media said, confirming widespread speculation over the polls which were last held in 2006. The vote will be held alongside presidential elections on September 11, 2027, Abbas said in a decree, blaming “obstacles” imposed by Israel, according to the Palestinian Wafa news agency. The legislative elections, which the international community has strongly advocated for, had been scheduled for November 28 this year, while a presidential vote was expected in early 2027. Israel had blasted Abbas’s Palestinian Authority as “corrupt” over the anticipated delay. “Abbas issued a presidential decree on Saturday calling for simultaneous presidential and legislative elections to be held on September 11, 2027,” Abbas’s office said in a statement published by Wafa . The presidency blamed the delay on “obstacles imposed by Israeli measures that prevent elections from being held on their previously scheduled date, as well as the need to create appropriate political, security and on-the-ground conditions to ensure free, fair and inclusive elections”. This week, Abbas’ Ramallah-based Palestinian Authority said Israel refused to allow Palestinian election officials access to east Jerusalem or Gaza ahead of the legislative elections. Israel’s foreign minister Gideon Saar on Friday had accused Abbas of “fooling the international community” by planning to postpone upcoming legislative polls. Holding polls is part of the reforms demanded by the international community for the Palestinian Authority, including the European Union. The last legislative elections in the Palestinian territories were held in 2006, when Hamas won. They defeated Fatah, which dominates the Palestinian Authority. The ensuing rift set off a round of factional fighting, with Hamas later seizing power in the Gaza Strip and creating a territorial divide between Fatah in the West Bank and Hamas in Gaza. As a result, the Palestinian Legislative Council, which is the Palestinian Authority’s parliament, has not met since 2007. Abbas won the last Palestinian presidential election in 2005, and his term should have expired in 2009, but he has since ruled by decree.

items.title: Ronaldo provisionally suspended by Portugal after team walkout
items.description: Cristiano Ronaldo has been provisionally suspended by the Portuguese Football Federation following the opening of disciplinary proceedings against the forward over his departure from the national team’s camp. Football journalist Fabrizio Romano shared the development in a post on X on Saturday, quoting an official statement from the federation confirming the decision. It reads, “The initiation of disciplinary proceedings against Cristiano Ronaldo, by deliberation of the Non-Professional Section, of October 9, 2026, with the purpose of the investigation of any disciplinary relevance of the facts participated on October 7 “Without prejudice to the automatic preventive suspension to which he was subject until the date of establishment, the non-automatic preventive suspension of the player was determined and the urgent nature was attributed to the process.” The latest decision follows Ronaldo’s departure from Portugal’s training camp on September 30 amid a disagreement with head coach Jorge Jesus. Ronaldo said he decided to leave after the coach allegedly failed to honour an agreement concerning his playing time and how the situation would be explained publicly. The dispute followed Portugal’s Nations League match against Norway, in which Ronaldo was an unused substitute despite warming up during the game. After leaving the camp, Ronaldo apologised to his teammates and Portuguese supporters, accepting responsibility for his actions and acknowledging that the federation should determine the consequences. The Al-Nassr forward is Portugal’s all-time leading scorer, with 146 international goals, and holds the national record for appearances, having represented his country 234 times. items.title: Dionewar : le centre culturel Cheikh Faty Faye, nouveau battement de cœur et levier de développement insulaire
items.description: Niché au cœur du delta du Sine Saloum, sur l’île de Dionewar, le nouveau Centre culturel Cheikh Faty Faye redéfinit le paysage local. Conçu comme un pont entre les cultures et un puissant outil de dynamisation économique, cet espace novateur répond à une urgence communautaire tout en misant sur l’écoconstruction. Le bâtiment est une architecture écoresponsable ancrée dans son milieu. Dressé entre mangrove et bolongs, le centre culturel Cheikh Faty Faye se distingue par ses choix architecturaux respectueux de l’environnement. Loin des standards standardisés, les bâtiments ont été façonnés à partir de matériaux écologiques locaux tels que le bloc de terre comprimée (BTC), le bois et la paille. L’ouvrage est une réponse parfaite au changement climatique. En réalité, il est conçu pour braver la chaleur, l'édifice intègre les contraintes thermiques et les besoins de ventilation de l'île. Selon Mamadou Sarr, alias Ass Ndank Ndank, président de l'association éponyme, l’ambition était d’offrir un lieu organique, pleinement intégré aux habitudes et aux aspirations de la communauté. Un projet né d'un besoin crucial Avant l'avènement de ce complexe, l’île de Dionewar souffrait d'un déficit criant d'infrastructures adaptées. Faute de cadre propice, la jeunesse, les femmes, les artisans et les artistes manquaient d'un point d'ancrage pour cultiver l'apprentissage, la création et le montage de projets. Ainsi, le projet a vu le jour grâce à la synergie impulsée par l’association « Ndank Ndank », en étroite collaboration avec les forces vives locales et des partenaires basques, sous l'égide de la coopération basque. Au-delà du soutien financier, cette initiative consacre une véritable démarche de réciprocité et d’échange interculturel. Au-delà, ce centre culturel est un carrefour d'expressions et de formation professionnelle. Car, à l'intérieur de ses murs, le centre déploie une riche palette d'infrastructures : une salle polyvalente pour les conférences, masterclass et projections, une bibliothèque, une galerie d'art, ainsi qu'un atelier de couture. Sa programmation culturelle fait la part belle au dialogue entre le Pays basque et le Sénégal. Qu'il s'agisse de séances de lutte traditionnelle, de ciné-forums ou d'ateliers artisanaux, la finalité demeure le partage d'expériences. « L’objectif n’est pas seulement de montrer une culture à l’autre, mais de créer des espaces de rencontre et d'apprentissage mutuel », souligne Mamadou Sarr. En plus de sa vocation artistique, le Centre culturel Cheikh Faty Faye se positionne comme un véritable catalyseur de croissance. C’est un endroit de création d’emplois. Sur ce, un atelier dédié aux artisans insuffle une dynamique professionnelle directe. Le site ambitionne aussi de structurer des filières de formation et de promouvoir un tourisme durable, respectueux du territoire insulaire et de ses habitants. En combinant effervescence artistique et opportunités économiques, ce centre s'impose d'ores et déjà comme la pierre angulaire du développement futur de Dionewar. M. DIEME

items.title: TOUMBA VA BIEN, LA RUMEUR NE TIENDRA PAS
items.description: Des mensonges et des informations diffamatoires circulent sur les réseaux sociaux au sujet de l’état de santé du Ministre d’État, Ministre de l’Intérieur, de la Sécurité publique et de l’Administration du territoire, le Général de Division Mohamed Toumba. Je tiens à les démentir formellement. J’ai personnellement rendu visite au Général de Division Mohamed Toumba en octobre 2026, à l’occasion de l’un de mes voyages. Je peux donc témoigner directement qu’il se porte bien, qu’il a retrouvé sa forme et qu’il demeure pleinement engagé dans ses responsabilités. Les informations alarmistes diffusées sur les réseaux sociaux ne correspondent pas à ce que j’ai moi-même constaté. Les activités publiques du Général Toumba au cours de ces derniers mois confirment également son engagement dans ses fonctions. En avril 2026, il s’est exprimé sur les activités de son département lors de l’exercice de redevabilité du Gouvernement. En mai, il a conduit la délégation nigérienne au Forum international sur la sécurité à Moscou. En juillet, il a participé aux échanges consacrés à la coopération sécuritaire de la Confédération des États du Sahel. En août, il présidait encore à Niamey une importante table ronde consacrée à la cohésion sociale et à la consolidation de la paix. Ces éléments permettent de mesurer l’écart entre la réalité et les mensonges actuellement diffusés. Une rumeur publiée sur les réseaux sociaux ne peut remplacer une observation directe, une activité officielle ou une information vérifiable. Il est particulièrement irresponsable de diffuser de tels mensonges et de se livrer à la diffamation sur l’état de santé d’une personnalité publique, au risque d’inquiéter inutilement sa famille, ses proches et l’opinion nationale. Le Général de Division Mohamed Toumba poursuit son engagement au service de l’État. Les informations concernant ses activités et son agenda continueront d’être connues à travers les canaux appropriés. J’invite chacun à faire preuve de discernement et à ne pas relayer des informations dont l’origine et la véracité ne sont pas établies. La vérité ne se construit pas sur les réseaux sociaux. Elle repose sur ce qui peut être vérifié. Par Ousmane Jazy L’article TOUMBA VA BIEN, LA RUMEUR NE TIENDRA PAS est apparu en premier sur Tamtaminfo .
